#Thank you for honoring the [Tenth Sabbath](/v/SavageGods/comments/889654).

There was a single transgression this time with a particular arbiter not honouring the sabbath. That post has been rejected. This was the third time something was posted during the Sabbath. And it's about time we're slightly more harsh.

This age is still the Age of Rebirth, as there have been no solid suggestions for new ages. Previously NobleParadox suggested something about dice influencing the game during this age, it was rejected.

The Age of Rebirth sounds to pretty to not have a game influencing rule. So please suggest one.

----------

##Welcome to Savage Gods!

Savage Gods is a collaborative storytelling game, with the idea that players are roleplaying a god, a species, or a hero character. The major drive behind the game is to play a game that is aimed at world / universe creation, and then playing within that creation.

Players have the ability to claim a god, by giving a name, and up to three domains of similar type. A domain is a declaration that a god holds power of said object or thing. Example; Suzy claims godhood as Reffika, goddess of Flowers, Weeds, and Greenery. Her most powerful influences would be on flowers and other such.

All races currently in the game have been created by a god, or multiple gods working together. This means that most races are theistic and believe in gods. Mostly because gods have been very hands on. However, if a race is claimed by a player, their direction and actions are completely dependent on what they want to do. Others can influence them, or have things happen, but it is up to the player how to interpret such influences or acts.

Hero characters are mostly champions, either brought forth by a god, or when a player only wanted to claim a single person, instead of an entire race. They have full autonomy over their character, though like with races, the gods can make things happen.

Overall though, no matter what you play, the intent of Savage Gods is to tell a big universal story together. There is no 'winning' in the sense that one person eventually will be victorious. We are all winning if we are enjoying the narrative we are telling. Remember, the more people get involved, the more fun the story gets.

If you want to play you might think it's a big step initially to join in, as the narrative grows quickly, stories are eligible for canonization after twenty hours, and thus there is much to read. You can do two things, find posts named 'The Sabbath' in this thread with the search function. Those contain weekly summaries by players, what their actions where. The alternative is to read the ecosystem, but if you're on a slow machine it might be punishing. (It consumes a ludicrous amount of RAM.) You can find the ecosystem [here](https://kumu.io/Phyra/ecosystem-of-gaea#gaea).

----------

##The Rules of SavageGods The rules below are guidelines, and not solid rules. They may be objected to, or followed to the letter. They are more like a *Pirate's Code* than they are the game rules. ###New players New players can claim a god, a race, or a hero character. You can have a race be created for you on request, or you can claim a race that already exists. If you claim an excising race, you can gain additional bonuses you cannot have when a new race is created. One of three bonuses, a demi-god character within your race, a leap of technology for your race as a starting boost, or a new opportunity to bless your race.

To claim an existing race or a hero character from an existing race, just make a post that introduces your character, or puts your claimage on said race. You can do this at any time during the game. We do ask that you hold to the creation mythos of said race, or hero character.

When you want to play a new race, make a post where you request a god (perhaps of a specific domain) to make said race for you. You can request attributes, special abilities, anything really that you want your race capable off. It's mostly up to other players, to agree if you get all your attributes, or perhaps if some get altered.

If you want to play a god, make a short post that introduces your god, and state up to three domains your god controls. These domains should have a tie in with eachother, or be of similar type.

When you claim your race, don't forget to give them a place on the [map](http://savagegods.net/gaea_political.svg). The map won't be updated right away, but at least everyone will know where you are. ###Gods As a god a player can create new things, or perform intricate actions. They can meddle with races, or send them on quests. The only limit is other gods that can oppose or influence your actions so that they either don't happen, or happen differently.

All players can vote on godly actions, other god players are welcomed to do so in game, and explain why they vote one way or another. However in the case of gods, influencing the action (positively or negatively) is preferred.

Races for obvious reasons cannot influence godly acts, but to keep things fair you have a meta vote. Do do a vote as a race, make sure you use [](#s "colored text"). Champions / hero characters are treated the same as races. ###Race Events As a race, species, or hero character, you can tell events and stories. Things that happened to your species, or a story line over several posts. You cannot influence the whole of creation as drastically as a god, but you have full control over the narrative you tell with your own race.

Other players can interact with your story, and alter the course, but in general race events / stories are more influenced based. Other races AND gods can introduce new elements, or alter elements that had been discussed. Gods can offer godly assistance, or godly wrath. Races can interact on a more level playing field, ###Relinquishing / Claiming Godhood So you're playing a god, but you'd rather play a race instead? No problem. Should a god feel the need, they may relinquish godhood and become a race/mortal/monster. They can create said mortals and relinquish godhood in the same post that includes the word 'relinquish' (or a form of it) in the title. This can trim our pantheon and create more races without having to rely too much on new players. Godhood can be reclaimed by the same player in the event that their mortal(s) die. Gods that have relinquished cannot abandon their own race. (No killing off your own race, just to become god again.) But if a god reclaims, they will be reinstated as if they were never gone. Domain, and divinity.'

Want to play a race, but not permanently relinquish godhood? That's okay too. If you wish to relinquish temporarily, you will still need to make a post. Temporary relinquishment can only claim available races. To reclaim godhood once you're done playing the race, you will need to make a reclaim post. You can only do this on the Sabbath or the start of the new age, and you will need to have played your race for at least 6 days.

You're not a god, but you want to become one? That's most certainly possible once again, however it's slightly more difficult. You will need to undergo a quest / story line that explains how your hero character became a demi-god, and from there an actual god. There haven't been much discussions on how to allow this, just that we should allow it now that gods can temporarily play races. If you are playing a race or hero, and you want to become a god, please try so! I am sure we'll figure things out as we go along. ###Arbitrage At this moment, when an event has been accepted into the story narrative, an arbiter will, after 20 hours and if the post is no longer part of an active discussion, flair the post and give a short summary of what went on in that post.

Once a post has a flair, it means it is locked, and should no longer be replied to in-game, unless an arbiter specifically states that 'it has a flair, but is still open to response'. By default, all council, parley, and meta actions will be flaired shortly after creation, but will still be open to responses.

When people have an argument about how to interpret past posts, or even current actions, arbiters will step in and decide for them. Though an arbiters word is not final. If at any time you disagree with an arbiter, you are more than welcome to present your argument, though you are asked to do so in a civil manner.

At this time, there are three arbiters, if ever you need one, tag all three of them in a post, the first to arrive will deal with the situation. @silvester, @NobleParadox, @Kith ###The Sabbath Every Monday the game holds a brief twenty hour respite. A time for everyone to focus instead on the Monday, and a time for those that do not play so often to catch up.

Each Sabbath will ask for a summary from the players what they did that week, together with links to said events or stories. The Sabbath is also a time to discuss new rules that might get implemented, and to decide what the next age will become.

The Sabbath thread will always be named 'The Sabbath' for easy search-ability.

----------

##Thank You That's about it for now, but this post is only a guideline set up by me - and that's not how things work around here. We're a group. If any of you have input, rules you would like altered, implemented, or things you would like to see in this post, please suggest them! This is a community, and we all need to agree on the rules / guidelines we hold ourselves by.
